title: Deprecate `dotutils.binlog-analyzer` in favor of `ms-dotnettools
body:
### Request

Please add a `deprecated` entry to the Marketplace extension-control manifest so that **`dotutils.binlog-analyzer`** shows the native "This extension is deprecated — use X instead" banner + **Migrate to …** button in the Extensions view, pointing users to the official Microsoft replacement.

This is the same UX as `ms-vscode.azure-account` → `ms-azuretools.vscode-azureresourcegroups`, and mirrors the author-initiated deprecation flow in #323176.

### Details

- **Extension to deprecate:** `dotutils.binlog-analyzer` (my personal publisher)
- **Replacement (official, same codebase, now shipped by Microsoft):** `ms-dotnettools.msbuild-binlog-analyzer` — "MSBuild Binlog Analyzer for VS Code" (published to the release channel, v1.0.1+)
- **Block new installs:** yes
- **Auto-migrate stored state:** yes, if supported

I own the `dotutils` publisher and am a contributor on the `ms-dotnettools` extension, so both sides of the migration are authorized.

### Proposed manifest entry

```json
"dotutils.binlog-analyzer": {
  "disallowInstall": true,
  "extension": {
    "id": "ms-dotnettools.msbuild-binlog-analyzer",
    "displayName": "MSBuild Binlog Analyzer for VS Code"
  },
  "autoMigrate": { "storage": true }
}
```

### Context

- #323176 (author-initiated deprecation flow)

title: Add rename_session to Agent Host session-management tools
body:
<!-- Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Summary

Add a `rename_session` operation to the existing Agent Host session-management tool group so an agent can rename its current session or a known session returned by `list_sessions`.

## Motivation

Agent Host sessions can already list, inspect, create, message, and delete sessions. They cannot directly rename the current or a specific session.

This limits workflows that organize long-running agent sessions. Initial auto-generated titles are often duplicated or become stale as the conversation evolves. A curator session should be able to periodically inspect idle sessions and apply meaningful titles without modifying conversation history.

## Existing workaround and verification

VS Code 1.131.0 already contains all the underlying mechanics:

- Session-management tools: `list_sessions`, `get_current_session`, `create_session`, `create_chat`, `send_message`, `get_session_context`, and `delete_session`:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1.131.0/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/sessionServerTools.ts
- `/rename <title>` is intercepted by `RenameLocalCommand`, dispatches `SessionTitleChanged`, and persists `customTitle`:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1.131.0/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/localCommands/renameLocalCommand.ts
- `SessionTitleChanged` is already a client-dispatchable action:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1.131.0/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/channels-session/actions.ts

I verified the workaround end-to-end on VS Code 1.131.0 (`e4c7e7b1d6d060162f4aa7f8225271b67ce1df75`):

1. A new Agent Host session whose first user message was `/rename <title>` persisted the requested `customTitle` and a completed rename-only turn.
2. A separate Agent Host session used `list_sessions` to find the target and `send_message` to send `/rename <new-title>`.
3. The target persisted the new title and completed rename-only turn after its VS Code window was closed.

The workaround proves cross-session rename is possible, but it has avoidable limitations:

- It cannot rename the current chat because `send_message` rejects self-targeting.
- It adds a synthetic `/rename` turn to the target transcript.
- It requires the broader `send_message` confirmation although only metadata changes.
- It does not expose a capability-aware error for providers that cannot rename, such as Cloud sessions.

## Proposed API

Add the following definition to the existing Agent Host session server tool group:

```json
{
  "name": "rename_session",
  "description": "Rename the current session or a known session.",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "session": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "Known session URI from list_sessions. Omit for the current session."
      },
      "title": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "New non-empty session title."
      }
    },
    "required": ["title"]
  }
}
```

Suggested behavior:

- Omitted `session` targets the current session.
- A provided `session` must resolve to a known URI from `list_sessions`.
- Validate and normalize the title before dispatch.
- Reuse `SessionTitleChanged` and the existing persistence path.
- Require confirmation when renaming another session.
- Return a capability-aware error when the provider does not support rename.
- Do not add a user/assistant turn to the target transcript.

## Use case

A dedicated session-title curator can periodically:

1. List idle, non-archived sessions.
2. Read recent context for sessions with duplicate or stale titles.
3. Suggest concise titles based on the current subject.
4. Rename only sessions whose title has materially drifted from their content.

This keeps the Sessions view useful as conversations change over time, while avoiding direct storage access and transcript pollution.

## Relationship to existing issues

- #288265 requested programmatic Copilot session rename and was closed in January 2026 because an extra standalone tool was not considered worth the cost. This proposal is narrower and is based on the Agent Host session-management tool group and persisted rename action now present in VS Code 1.131.0. That issue is locked, so the new implementation context cannot be added there.
- #308104 proposed a broad extension-facing CRUD API for all chat sessions and was closed after the feature-request upvote period. This proposal does not request that broad Extension API.
- #318855 requests read-only session observation APIs for extensions. This proposal is an Agent Host mutation operation and complements that read-side request.

## Acceptance criteria

- An Agent Host session can rename itself without sending a synthetic chat turn.
- An Agent Host session can rename another known rename-capable session after confirmation.
- Unsupported session types fail without changing state.
- The updated title is immediately visible and persists after window reload/restart.

title: Environment variables from the first VS Code launch carry over to later windows

Type: Bug ## Description VS Code keeps a shared main process running across windows. When the first window starts with an environment variable, the main process keeps that value. Later windows inherit the same value, even when they open unrelated directories. It remains visible in their integrated terminals unless it is overwritten. For example, a developer loads an LLM API key into the current environment. They then launch VS Code with `code` to debug an AI agent. The key unexpectedly appears in other newly opened VS Code windows. ## Steps to Reproduce (using `code-insiders` instead of `code`) 1. title: AHP listSessions mappers silently drop optional wire fields
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

The AHP `root/listSessions` payload is mapped by two independent, hand-written, field-by-field object literals:

- **producer** — `SessionSummary` built in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts`
- **consumer** — `IAgentSessionMetadata` built in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/remoteAgentHostProtocolClient.ts`

Neither is exhaustive over `SessionSummary`, and `satisfies SessionSummary` does **not** flag a missing *optional* property. An optional field added to the protocol is therefore silently dropped by either side with no compile error and no test failure. The provider-level tests can't catch it either: `MockAgentHostService.listSessions` returns its stored metadata verbatim and bypasses both mappers entirely.

This has already produced the same user-visible bug twice. Workspace-less quick chats carry their `agentHost.workspaceless` marker on `_meta`; both mappers dropped `_meta`; so any quick chat first materialized from a listing (window reload, list refresh) was classified as a workspace session rooted at the host's throwaway `~/.copilot/chats/<id>` scratch dir, and the sessions sidebar grouped it under a section header labelled with a raw session UUID instead of under "Chats". Fixed for `_meta` in fe8a00d9d51 — but the trap itself is still armed. `annotations?: AnnotationsSummary` is on the wire today and dropped by the consumer; it has no client consumer yet, so it is latent rather than broken.

### Proposal

Make the drift impossible to reintroduce at compile time:

1. **Producer** — annotate the wire item with a mapped type that strips optionality, e.g. `{ [K in keyof SessionSummary]-?: SessionSummary[K] | undefined }`, forcing every field to be named. Every transport serializes (WebSocket JSON, IPC channel, relay), so an explicitly-`undefined` key is indistinguishable from an absent one on the wire, and the mapper already writes `activity`, `workingDirectories` and `changes` in exactly that style.
2. **Consumer** — destructure `SessionSummary` exhaustively with a rest element constrained to be empty, so a newly added wire field fails the build until the client decides whether it needs it.

### Why not just add a round-trip test

The producer is in the `node` layer and the consumer is in `browser`, so no single test can import both without violating layering (there is no precedent for that in the existing tests). A round-trip test would also only ever protect the fields it happens to cover, whereas the type-level guards cover every future field.

### Related

The deeper coupling worth revisiting separately: the host puts a throwaway scratch cwd on the wire as a real `workingDirectories` entry and then ships the "ignore it" signal out-of-band in a generic `_meta` bag. Making workspace-less-ness a first-class field of the session summary would remove the need for the marker to survive the mapping at all.

title: Queued GitHub Copilot commands merged and use wrong model.
body:
1. Issue the command `/compact`.
2. While the conversation is being compacted, issue a custom prompt `/foo` with Model A selected, and press `<Enter>`. The prompt will be queued.
3. While the conversation is still being compacted, issue a custom prompt `/bar` with Model B selected, and press `<Enter>`. The prompt will also be queued.

**Expected:** When the conversation is finished being compacted, prompt `/foo` will be submitted using Model A; and when it is finished prompt `/bar` will be submitted using Model B.

**Actual:** When the conversation is finished being compacted, prompt `/foo` and prompt `/bar` are combined into a single prompt and submitted using Model A.

This is blatantly wrong on many fronts:

* The prompts should have been submitted separately because they were queued separately; if I would have wanted them combined, I would have submitted them combined.
* The result of combining the prompts means that **`/bar` wasn't even recognized as a custom prompt** and instead was apparently submitted as the literal test `/bar` in the body of the combined prompt. (At least `/bar` was not displayed as being recognized as a custom prompt.)
* The second prompt, `/bar`, needed a more powerful model, Model B. If I would have wanted to use Model A for `/bar`, I would have selected Model A instead of Model B.

<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.129.1
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open two or more integrated terminals so the terminal tabs list is visible.
2. In one of them, run:

   ```bash
   i=0; while :; do i=$((i + 1)); printf '\033]0;working-%06d\007' "$i"; sleep 0.05; done
   ```

3. While it is running, use the trash, split, or rename action in the terminal tabs list.

Actual behavior:

- Trash and split do nothing.
- Rename opens briefly and immediately closes.
- Context-menu **Kill Terminal** and the Command Palette kill command still work.
- The actions work again after stopping the loop with `Ctrl+C`.

Expected behavior:

Terminal tab actions remain usable during title updates.

Additional information:

This was first noticed with Codex CLI 0.144.6: it occurs while Codex is working and stops when Codex becomes idle. These settings do not prevent it:

```json
"terminal.integrated.tabs.allowAgentCliTitle": false,
"terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled": false
```

Related: [#279443: Rename Terminal Immediately Exits](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/279443) — closed as not planned, but the reproduction above may explain its root cause.

title: MCP model access permissions fail silently, making working servers appear broken
body:
Describe the feature you’d like

When an MCP server requires model access (for example, to perform sampling), VS Code should explicitly notify the user if the currently selected model has not been granted permission to be used by that MCP server.

Currently, this failure is difficult to discover. From the user’s perspective, the MCP server appears to be malfunctioning, even though the actual issue is simply a missing model access permission.

This is especially confusing because:

* The MCP server starts successfully.
* The server is visible in VS Code.
* Tools may even be listed correctly.
* There is no obvious indication that the selected model is not allowed to access the server.

As a result, many users naturally assume that:

* the MCP server is broken,
* OAuth or authentication is misconfigured,
* or the MCP implementation itself has a bug.

Only users who already know about Configure Model Access are likely to identify the real cause.

Expected behavior

Instead of failing silently, VS Code should provide a clear and actionable message such as:

This MCP server is not permitted to use the selected model.

Actions could include:

* Grant Access
* Configure Model Access

or automatically open the model access configuration dialog.

Why this would help

The current security model makes sense—requiring explicit permission before an MCP server can use a model is a reasonable default.

The issue is discoverability, not security.

A clear permission prompt or error message would significantly improve the onboarding and debugging experience while preserving the existing security model.

Instead of spending time debugging a perfectly healthy MCP server, users would immediately understand that the missing permission is the only issue.

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

I've been using `singlePaneDetailPanel` for a bit now, and while I like the overall structure and approach, there are some issues that frustrated my experience. I imagine some are just small bugs in the preview, others maybe tweaks.

### 1 - Files keeps being closed
I want to quickly switch to files, check things, then revert to changes, and so on. Problem is: Files keeps closing. The reason is that "Files" switches to the individual file once I select it, so when I close, the Files tab is gone. While I can see the logic that "well it's opening one file", the fact the window is presented with the tree view on the side, it's effective how one would also browse files.

Steps:
1. Open the "Files" tab
2. Select one file
3. I'm done, close the file
4. Outcome: the files tree is now gone, and I've to re-add it as a tab.

An idea: barred larger flow fixes, one idea would simply be that if the file is pinned, when closed, it restores the empty "Files" selector instead of closing the tab.

### 2 - Changes show just one file
I appreciate the view with the full list of changes as a single list. For some things it's great. But when I want to see only one file, I keep accidentally scrolling too far in either direction, which is frustrating.

Steps:
1. Open the "Changes" view
2. Click on one specific file in the tree/list view
3. Outcome: scrolls to a file

An idea: provide a way to switch from a single list of all changes, to changes one-file-at-time so it can't scroll away (similar to how collapse all / expand all happens). Having a quick toggle like that would help switching view easily depending on the need / task.

title: Chat: Subagent transcript items trigger potential listener leak warning
body:
### Description

Opening an Agents window transcript with many surfaced subagent chats can trigger this DevTools warning:

```text
[120] potential listener LEAK detected, having 204 listeners already. MOST frequent listener (23)
```

The most frequent listener stack points through `ChatSubagentContentPart._updateOpenChatLink`, `MenuWorkbenchToolBar`, and `MenuImpl.onDidChange`.

### Reproduction steps

1. Open an Agents window session whose transcript contains many subagent tool invocations with surfaced subagent chats.
2. Let the transcript render, or scroll so its response rows rerender.
3. Open the developer tools console.
4. Observe the potential listener leak warning.

### Expected behavior

Rendered subagent transcript items should not each add a persistent listener to the shared context-key change event.

### Actual behavior

Every subagent with an openable chat creates a persistent `MenuWorkbenchToolBar` for `MenuId.ChatSubagentContent`. The toolbar listens to its `MenuImpl`, which consequently installs a listener on the shared context-key event. Completed subagent parts remain rendered in the transcript, so the listener count grows with the number of subagents and crosses the leak-warning threshold.

### Confirmed root cause

The rendered parts are correctly disposed when replaced or removed. The warning is instead caused by architectural listener fan-out: one persistent menu, and therefore one shared context-key listener, per retained `ChatSubagentContentPart`.

The subagent action is static after contribution registration, so it can be resolved using a one-shot `IMenuService.getMenuActions` snapshot and rendered in a plain `WorkbenchToolBar`. The late action-view registration race only needs a self-removing listener.

title: Agent Host session returns to plan mode after plan approval and reload
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Start an Agent Host session in Plan mode.
2. Let the agent create a plan.
3. Accept the plan and choose an implementation mode such as Interactive.
4. Let the agent finish, then reload or reopen the session later.

## Expected

The session remains in the mode selected when the plan was accepted.

## Actual

The session returns to Plan mode after it is restored.

## Root cause

Plan acceptance correctly updates the live AHP session config through a server-dispatched `session/configChanged` action. However, merged session config values are persisted only from the client-action side-effect path. Server-originated mode changes therefore update the picker and live state but leave the persisted `configValues.mode` as `plan`, which is restored on reload.

Session-config persistence should observe applied action envelopes regardless of whether the action originated from a client or the server.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Modern UI (floating-panels) forces status bar background transparent, breaking statusBar.background color customizations
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **Yes** (reproducible with pure `settings.json`, no extensions)

- VS Code Version: 1.131.0-insider (commit `29215ba85809234979befc6b0d1fb4b0ab884383`)
- OS Version: macOS 15.7.7 (arm64)

### Summary

When the **`workbench.experimental.modernUI`** experiment is active (staged rollout — `experiment: { mode: "auto" }`), the workbench switches to the `floating-panels` layout, which forces the status bar background to `transparent !important`. This overrides any user or extension `workbench.colorCustomizations` for `statusBar.background`, so the customization is applied but never visible.

This silently breaks status bar coloring for users and for popular extensions that rely on `statusBar.background` — e.g. **[Peacock](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=johnpapa.vscode-peacock)** (cc @johnpapa) and [Lantern](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=sinedied.lantern).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On an Insiders build enrolled in the `workbench.experimental.modernUI` experiment (or set `"workbench.experimental.modernUI": true`).
2. Add to `settings.json`:
   ```json
   "workbench.colorCustomizations": {
     "statusBar.background": "#ff00ff"
   }
   ```
3. Observe the status bar stays the theme default (transparent floating bar) instead of magenta.
4. Set `"workbench.experimental.modernUI": false` → magenta appears as expected.

### Root cause

The `floating-panels` stylesheet injects an `!important` rule that beats the inline background the theming layer sets on the status bar part:

```css
.monaco-workbench.floating-panels .part.activitybar,
.monaco-workbench.floating-panels .part.statusbar,
.monaco-workbench.floating-panels .part.titlebar {
  background-color: transparent !important;
  border-color: transparent !important;
}
```

Inspecting the live DOM confirms the customization *is* applied but overridden:

- `<footer id="workbench.parts.statusbar">` → inline style `background-color: rgb(255, 0, 255)` (customization honored)
- `getComputedStyle(...).backgroundColor` → `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` (transparent, due to the `!important` rule)
- Workbench classes include `floating-panels style-override`

In modern UI the status bar part is only ever tinted through an internal "style override" path, using `statusBar.debuggingBackground` at 30% opacity:

```css
.monaco-workbench.floating-panels .part.statusbar.has-style-override {
  background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--vscode-statusBar-debuggingBackground) 30%, transparent) !important;
}
```

There is no equivalent path for the normal `statusBar.background`, and extensions cannot opt a part into `has-style-override`.

### Impact / notes

- Not a regression of the theme-color surface itself — `statusBar.background` etc. are unchanged between 1.130 stable and 1.131. The behavior change is purely the injected CSS in the `floating-panels` layout.
- Status bar **item** backgrounds (e.g. `statusBarItem.errorBackground`, `prominentBackground`) still render, so item-based coloring is unaffected; only the whole-bar `statusBar.background` is suppressed.
- Because this ships via staged experiment, affected users see it "spontaneously" break with no settings change, which makes it hard to diagnose.

### Question / request

Is suppressing `statusBar.background` intended in modern UI? If so, could there be a supported way for users/extensions to color the floating status bar (e.g. honor `statusBar.background` via the same `color-mix` treatment, or a documented opt-in), so extensions like Peacock and Lantern can adapt?

title: Agents window Markdown editor: macOS word and line navigation use the wrong modifiers
body:
<!-- Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template -->

Testing #326540

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: Insiders with the experimental Markdown editor
- OS Version: macOS
- Audited package revision: microsoft/vscode-packages@1d81418d61ad769f154579196a51a9364c105e2d

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Markdown document containing `alpha beta gamma` in **Editing** mode.

3. Try the standard macOS editing commands:
   - Option+Left
   - Option+Backspace
   - Cmd+Left
   - Cmd+Backspace
   - Cmd+Up

### Expected

- Option+Left and Option+Backspace operate on the previous word.
- Cmd+Left and Cmd+Backspace operate to the start of the visual line.

### Actual

- Cmd+Left and Cmd+Backspace operate on the previous word.
- Cmd+Up does not move the caret.

### Impact

The editor breaks platform muscle memory and differs from both native macOS text controls and VS Code's normal editor. Keyboard-driven users must slow down and can delete the wrong amount of text. This is especially disruptive for accessibility workflows that rely on predictable keyboard navigation.

title: fix: guard null visibleRangeForPosition in indent guides (fixes #244370)
body:
### Summary Rendering indent guides crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'left')` in `IndentsOverlay.prepareRender`. The code asserts `ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(...)!.left` non-null, but that method legitimately returns `HorizontalPosition | null` when the requested position is not in the currently rendered range (e.g. during scrolling, wrapped lines, or a stale layout). When it returns `null`, the `!` assertion dereferences null and throws, aborting the whole view render pass. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#244370 Recommended reviewer: `@hediet` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`78cb0b490a60`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/78cb0b490a60) | | Author | `@hediet` | | PR | (not identified) | | Message | Indent guides rendering (bracket pair guides) | | Why | This commit introduced the `ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(new Position(lineNumber, guide.column))!.left` expression at the crash site. The `!` non-null assertion bypasses the method's declared `HorizontalPosition \| null` return type; whenever the position is outside the rendered range the value is `null` and the dereference throws. This is a long-standing (pre-existing, 2022) latent bug rather than a recent regression. | > Pre-existing latent bug: `git blame` dates the offending line to 2022. Telemetry re-surfaces it intermittently because it only fires when `visibleRangeForPosition` returns `null` for a non-`-1` guide column during a render pass. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant View as EditorView.render participant Overlay as IndentsOverlay.prepareRender participant Ctx as RenderingContext.visibleRangeForPosition View->>Overlay: prepareRender(ctx) Overlay->>Ctx: visibleRangeForPosition(Position(line, guide.column)) Note over Ctx: Returns null when the
position is not in the
rendered range Ctx-->>Overlay: null Note over Overlay: 💥 (null)!.left throws:
Cannot read properties of null ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/indentGuides/indentGuides.ts` | crash site & root cause | L137-139 (from stack): `ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(new Position(lineNumber, guide.column))!.left` — `!` bypasses the nullable return | | `src/vs/editor/browser/view/renderingContext.ts` | producer (correctly typed) | L102-103: `visibleRangeForPosition(position): HorizontalPosition \| null { return this._viewLines.visibleRangeForPosition(position) ?? this._viewLinesGpu?.visibleRangeForPosition(position) ?? null; }` | ### Repro Steps Non-deterministic — depends on the renderer returning `null` for a guide column position while indent/bracket-pair guides are enabled. 1. Enable bracket pair / indentation guides (default). 2. Open a large file and scroll rapidly, or trigger a layout where a guide's column falls outside the currently rendered line range (wrapped lines, partially rendered viewport). 3. When `visibleRangeForPosition` returns `null` for a guide's column during `prepareRender`, the non-null assertion throws. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/indentGuides/indentGuides.ts`: replace the `!.left` non-null assertion with an explicit null check. When `visibleRangeForPosition` returns `null` for a guide's column, `continue` to skip that single guide instead of dereferencing null. The method's declared return type is already `HorizontalPosition | null`, and the immediately surrounding code already treats null as a normal outcome (L132 uses `?.left ?? 0`; L152-154 uses `?.left ?? (left + this._spaceWidth)`). title: NES: gutter indicator menu lacks ARIA menu semantics and arrow-key navigation
body:
Found while doing a hands-on accessibility pass over Next Edit Suggestions. Related to #327616 (which covers reaching the menu at all).

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No — NES requires the GitHub Copilot extension to provide the inline edit.

- VS Code Version: 1.132.0 (built from source, `3ddd267c500`)
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.60.0
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Trigger a next edit suggestion and hover the gutter indicator to open its menu (**Go To / Accept**, **Reject**, **Show Collapsed**, **Snooze**, **Settings**, **Feedback**).
2. Inspect the menu items.

## Actual

The menu is a custom construction that does not expose ARIA menu semantics:

- Items are `div.monaco-menu-option` with `tabIndex: 0` but **no `role="menuitem"`**.
- There is **no `role="menu"` container**, so the items are not grouped as a menu and the item count/position is not conveyed.
- Items have **no `aria-label`**; the accessible name is only the concatenated text plus the keybinding label.
- Keyboard handling is **<kbd>Enter</kbd> only** — no <kbd>Space</kbd>, and no <kbd>Up</kbd>/<kbd>Down</kbd> arrow navigation. Users must <kbd>Tab</kbd> through each item individually, which is not the expected menu interaction model.

## Cause

`src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/components/gutterIndicatorMenu.ts`

```ts
function option(props: { ... }) {
    return derived({ name: 'inlineEdits.option' }, (_reader) => n.div({
        class: ['monaco-menu-option', props.isActive?.map(v => v && 'active')],
        onmouseenter: ...,
        onmouseleave: ...,
        onclick: props.onAction,
        onkeydown: e => {
            if (e.key === 'Enter') {
                props.onAction?.();
            }
        },
        tabIndex: 0,
        ...
```

## Expected

Either adopt the existing menu widget (which already handles roles, arrow navigation and typeahead), or add `role="menu"` on the container, `role="menuitem"` on the options, arrow-key navigation, and <kbd>Space</kbd> activation.

title: Markdown Editor (Experimental) Breaks When Markdown Metadata Is Present
body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.130.0 - OS Version: 26.5.2 Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open a new Markdown file (`tmp.md`) in the VS Code Editor using the Experimental Markdown Editor view (`vscode.markdown.preview.editor`). 2. Paste the following YAML front matter containing nested lists and sub-objects at the top of the file: ```markdown --- number: "01" title: "title" list: - "one" - "two" double: - first: "here" second: here - first: "here" second: "here" --- # Hello * World * This is me ``` ### Actual Result (Editor View) The editor breaks the structural YAML layout. It strips out the indentation, merges key-value boundaries, and turns the sub-lists into a confusing mix of flat bullet points and inline strings on a single line (e.g., rendering `number: "01" title: "title" list:` entirely on one compressed line, followed by malformed bullets). Here's a screenshot of the Markdown Editor (Experimental) in edit mode: ### Expected Result The block should either preserve its native YAML formatting structure inside the editor canvas, or cleanly inherit the exact rendering engine behavior used by the **Markdown Preview panel**, which cleanly separates and tables complex structural metadata. Here's a screenshot of the Markdown Preview (not the Experimental Editor): ### Additional Context The standard side-by-side Markdown Preview parses this identical snippet flawlessly. The layout breakdown is isolated exclusively to the Markdown Editor canvas implementation when interacting with nested YAML structures.

title: Agents session disappears after switching away from a failed session with an active fork
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.59.2026072302
- VS Code Version: 1.131.0-insider (9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04, arm64)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window, Copilot CLI multi-chat/forked chat, Sessions sidebar
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Reproduced and correlated in local Agent Host, AHP, renderer, and profile-storage logs. Relevant event sequence and conclusions are included below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In the Agents window Sessions filter, leave **Failed** unchecked (the persisted profile value is `sessionsListControl.excludedStatuses = [4]`, where `4` is UI `SessionStatus.Error`).
2. Open a Copilot CLI session and let its default/main chat fail.
3. Fork the chat before the failure point and continue working in the fork so the peer chat is actively `InProgress`.
4. Observe that the active session remains visible in the sidebar, but its row is labelled **Failed** even while the fork is running.
5. Switch to another session.
6. Observe that the original session immediately disappears from the Sessions sidebar.
7. Re-enable **Failed** or reset the Sessions filters; the session reappears.

## Expected

A running peer/fork chat should promote the aggregate session status to `InProgress`, matching the Sessions contract (`NeedsInput > InProgress > other`). Switching away should therefore leave the still-running session visible when only Failed sessions are excluded.

See - https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C09MVCZKLP4/p1784823824073999?thread_ts=1784823693.032779&cid=C09MVCZKLP4

## Actual

The aggregate session remains `Error` while the peer chat is running. Because Failed sessions are excluded, the row is visible only while active and disappears as soon as another session becomes active. This looks like destructive session loss, although the session, chats, and worktree are still present.

## Root Cause Analysis

There are three interacting behaviors:

1. `AgentHostStateManager._aggregateChatSummaries` in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts` checks `errorChat` before `inProgressChat`, giving the effective precedence `InputNeeded > Error > InProgress`. When the default chat has failed and a peer fork starts streaming, the session summary therefore remains `Error`.
2. `SessionsList.update` in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts` filters sessions whose status is in `excludedStatuses`.
3. The same method deliberately reinserts a filtered session while it is active. Once the user switches sessions, that exception no longer applies and the Error-status session vanishes from the list.

The multi-chat status implementation conflicts with `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`, which documents `NeedsInput > InProgress > other`. Existing tests cover a running peer with an **idle** default chat, but not a running peer with an **errored** default chat.

## Log Evidence

- The default chat transitioned to protocol `Error`.
- The forked peer chat subsequently transitioned to protocol `InProgress`.
- No aggregate session-summary transition to `InProgress` was emitted while the fork ran.
- A later `listSessions` response still contained the session with `Error | IsRead`; there was no delete, archive, or dispose request.

## Suggested Fix

Change the aggregate precedence to `InputNeeded > InProgress > Error`, then add a regression test where:

1. the default chat is Error;
2. a peer chat starts and the session becomes InProgress;
3. the peer completes and the session falls back to Error.

A secondary UX improvement would be to make active status filters more obvious, since the active-session exception currently masks the filter until navigation.

title: Convert `file://vscode-app` links to `code` Markdown when pasting in GitHub Copilot chat.
body:
Half the things I select and copy and paste in GitHub Copilot chat turn into links in the form:

```markdown
There might be a [foo-bar.md](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/user/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/…/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) file somewhere.
```

This gets in the way of copy-and-paste all the time. It's irritating, and I have to wind up deleting it and pasting as plain text, which removes _all_ the markup.

What's worse is that **`foo-bar.md` should not even had a link in the first place**. They don't point to anything, and the file in question didn't even exist in the repository. This is an irritating, compounding separate issue that shows up because of #297792 and #297792. The bug is on two levels:

1. The GitHub copilot chat is buggy because it adds adds links that shouldn't be there (#280165 and #297792).
2. The Markdown propagates those links when I paste.

The chat cruft is bad enough, but now it affects everything I paste.

**Fix:** When pasting Markdown, if a link node is encountered using a URL with a `vscode-file` scheme, interpret the link as if it were a `code` node producing a Markdown backtick-delimited span.

This issue is more onerous to the user than it sounds. Please add this simple little fix.

This paste fix will probably be found in the past-as-Markdown code that was improved in #319733 , which @lramos15 did [a great job](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/319733#issuecomment-4682849884) on by quickly responding to feedback and making the design more elegant and maintainable.

body:

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: Version: 1.130.0 (Universal) 1b6a188127eeaf9194f945eb6eb89a657e93c54c
- OS Version: macOS 15.x (Apple Silicon)

When the `ChatAllowedMcpServers` enterprise policy (chat.mcp.allowedServers) is
active, a remote (HTTP) MCP server that is EXPLICITLY ALLOWED by a `serverUrl`
matcher starts but never finishes initializing — it stays in "Running" / loops
"Waiting for server to respond to initialize request..." and never discovers
tools. Removing the policy (no other change) lets the identical URL connect and
discover tools in ~2s.
This is NOT limited to OAuth. It reproduces with:
  * a public NO-AUTH remote server (DeepWiki, https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp), and
Both are allowed by the policy, yet neither completes initialization while the policy is active.
`serverCommand`-matched stdio servers work fine under the same policy.
### Policy value (macOS managed preference com.microsoft.VSCode → ChatAllowedMcpServers)
[
  {"serverUrl":"https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp"}
]
### mcp.json
{
  "servers": {
    "deepwiki":     { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp" }
  }
}

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Deploy the ChatAllowedMcpServers policy above.
2. Fully quit + relaunch VS Code.
3. Start "deepwiki" (public, no auth) → it sits at "Running" and never
   discovers tools.
4. Retract the policy, relaunch, start the same servers with no other change → connect (DeepWiki discovers 3 tools in <2s).
### Logs
POLICY ON — DeepWiki (no auth) never initializes:
  15:29:21  Starting server deepwiki / Connection state: Running
  15:29:33  (restart) Running
  15:36:40  (restart) Running
  15:37:37  Extension host shut down — never "Discovered tools"
POLICY OFF — same DeepWiki URL works:
  15:37:44  Starting server deepwiki / Running
  15:37:46  Discovered 3 tools

### Expected
A server allowed by chat.mcp.allowedServers via `serverUrl` behaves identically
to no policy: it initializes and discovers tools.
### Actual
Any remote server matched by `serverUrl` fails to initialize while the policy
is active, whether or not it uses OAuth. Only `serverCommand` (stdio) servers
work under the policy.

title: Feature Request: Allow folding single physical lines that are soft-wrapped via wordWrap
body: ## Feature Request ### Problem VS Code's folding mechanism only works for multi-line blocks separated by hard newlines. When a **single physical line** is long enough to trigger `editor.wordWrap` (soft visual wrapping): - The line renders as multiple wrapped display lines on screen - No folding arrow appears in the gutter - Users cannot collapse this entire single physical line ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Editor settings: ```json "editor.wordWrap": "bounded", "editor.wordWrapColumn": 120 ``` 2. Create a file containing **only one physical line** (no manual hard line breaks): ```python OPENAI_KEY = "sk-proj-1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111" ``` 3. Resize editor window to trigger soft wrapping. 4. Observe: no fold arrow appears in the gutter for this line. ### Pain Points 1. Many scenarios use long single-line literals: API keys, tokens, long URLs, long string constants. 2. We enable wordWrap to eliminate horizontal scrollbars, but cannot hide these long lines. 3. Current mandatory workarounds: - Modify source code to split the single line into a multi-line expression block to gain foldability. - Install third-party extensions like Inline Fold for line-in text collapsing. Neither workaround is ideal. ### Expected Behavior Single physical lines that are visually soft-wrapped should support native folding: 1. Render fold indicator in the gutter for the single physical line 2. Click to collapse the whole physical line 3. Show shortened preview after collapse (e.g. `OPENAI_KEY = "..."`) ### Additional Context The core limitation: folding logic only parses hard newline boundaries, and does not treat soft-wrapped display lines as foldable ranges.

title: MCP App webviews duplicate identical multi-MB HTML bundles (35MB in one renderer snapshot)
body:
Found while analyzing a renderer heap snapshot from the Agents window (484 MB self-size).

## Summary

**16 `<!DOCTYPE html>` strings totalling 35.2 MB** were retained via `WebviewElement._content.html`. They are only **two distinct MCP App bundles**, byte-identical, duplicated **11× and 5×** respectively — each ~2.2 MB of HTML with inlined JS.

The snapshot contained **32 live `ChatMcpAppModel` instances**, each with its own `WebviewElement`, plus 33 `ChatToolInvocationWebviewPart`.

## Cause

`ChatMcpAppModel._loadContent()` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatMcpAppModel.ts:216-241`):

```ts
const resourceContent = await this._mcpToolCallUI.loadResource(token);
...
const htmlWithCsp = this._injectPreamble(resourceContent);
...
this._webview.setHtml(htmlWithCsp);
```

Every chat turn that invokes the same MCP app loads the resource again and allocates a **fresh flat copy** of the injected HTML. `WebviewElement._content.html` (`webviewElement.ts:137`) then retains it for the element's lifetime — it's needed by `reload()` / `reinitializeAfterDismount()` — and is never cleared on dispose.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Intern the bundle.** Cache the result of `_injectPreamble` keyed by resource URI + CSP (in `McpToolCallUI` or the resource loader). JS strings are immutable, so all 16 webviews can share one instance: **35 MB → 2.2 MB**, for the cost of a small cache. This is the real fix.
2. **Defensively clear `_content.html` in `WebviewElement.dispose()`.** Cheap, but only helps if some of these 32 models were already disposed. Worth checking either way — 32 simultaneously-live MCP App webviews in one window seems high, and if some are disposed-but-retained there's a second bug here.

## Effort estimate

Easy, and a good return: ~33 MB recovered in this snapshot, and it scales with how heavily MCP Apps get used.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Built-in skills are not returned by the sessionless commands.list API (skills unavailable in sessionless chat input completions)
body:
## Summary

The sessionless `commands.list()` API does not return built-in skills. As a result, skills are **not available in the sessionless chat input completions** — they only become available **after a session has been created**.

## Details

- The sessionless `commands.list()` API filters returned commands to those flagged `availableAtSessionStart`.
- Skills are always `availableAtSessionStart: false`, so **no skills appear in that RPC at all** (including built-in skills bundled with the runtime).
- Skills are instead surfaced through a separate API surface — `skills.discover` / `session.skills.list()` and the `session.skills_loaded` event — all of which require (or are tied to) a loaded session.

## Impact

- When a user has not yet created a session (i.e. the sessionless chat input), skill slash commands do not show up in input completions.
- Built-in skills in particular are effectively invisible until a session exists, which is surprising because they ship with the runtime and could reasonably be offered at session start.
- This creates an inconsistent completion experience: built-in commands (e.g. runtime commands) are completable pre-session, but skills are not.

## Expected

Skills (at minimum built-in skills) should be discoverable/completable in the sessionless chat input, or there should be a documented, intentional reason why skill completions require a session.

## Notes

The implementing repository is private, so this issue captures the behavior at a conceptual level rather than linking source. Happy to provide more detail on request.

body:
Refs: #324825, #327067

- [x] macOS @bryanchen-d 
- [x] linux @deepak1556 
- [x] windows @jruales 

Complexity: 4

---

Verify that Agent Host Copilot streams output from the Copilot SDK built-in shell tool live in the chat terminal UI.

Prerequisites:
- Use the latest VS Code Insiders
- Sign in to GitHub Copilot
- Enable `chat.agentHost.enabled`
- Set `chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled` to `false` so Agent Host uses the Copilot SDK built-in shell tool

Part 1: Command output
- Start an Agent Host Copilot session
- Ask the agent: "Run something that prints a random number every second for the next 20 seconds"
- The agent can use a command such as:
  ```sh
  for i in $(seq 1 20); do echo "[$i] $RANDOM"; sleep 1; done
  ```
- Confirm each numbered result appears progressively while the command is running instead of all output appearing after completion
- Confirm the terminal UI automatically expands while new output is arriving
- Confirm the command changes from running to completed when it finishes

Part 2: Successful and failing commands
- Run a command that succeeds and confirm its completed state reflects a successful exit
- Run a command that exits with a non-zero status and confirm its completed state reflects the failure
- Confirm the final output remains visible and readable after both commands complete

Part 3: Output integrity
- Run commands that produce:
  - multiple output lines
  - enough output to exercise retained or truncated output
- Confirm output is not duplicated, reordered, stale, or missing
- Confirm output from one shell call does not appear in another shell call
- Confirm the final completed output is consistent with what was shown while the command was running

Part 4: Completed output and session history
- Run several terminal commands in the same Agent Host Copilot session
- Collapse and expand completed shell calls and confirm their output is preserved
- Reload the window or resume the session and confirm completed shell output is restored correctly
- Confirm completed output does not create an additional terminal in the Terminal panel

Part 5: Exploratory
- Use the built-in shell naturally during an Agent Host Copilot coding session
- Try commands that produce ongoing output, such as builds, tests, and `npm install`
- Note any cases where:
  - output does not appear until the command completes
  - output is duplicated, stale, reordered, or missing
  - a completed command continues to appear as running
  - completed output disappears after reload or resume
  - a built-in shell call unexpectedly creates a terminal in the Terminal panel

title: GitHub Copilot `file_search` truncation can cause false “file does not exist” conclusions
body:
GitHub Copilot `file_search` result truncation consistently trips up models. **This is a recurring problem and the results misguide models.** A model such as GPT-5.6 Luna is completely capable of a simple task of loading the context window with relevant context. However if there are many files, the `file_search` tool just truncates results and **does not provide sufficient notice to the model that results were truncated and that more results are available**. Instead, the model comes away with the impression that some of the files it was looking for does not exist.

Below is the explanation in the words of GPT-5.6 Sol:

# `file_search` truncation is not reported explicitly enough

## Description

A prompt requested loading several project-context artifacts, including an active work item's description, while skipping targets that do not exist.

I searched the work item's directory using a recursive glob:

```text
path/to/work-item/**
```

I omitted `maxResults`, expecting the returned file list to be sufficient for determining which requested artifacts existed.

The tool reported the total number of matches, displayed only a subset, and ended the output with `...`. Because truncation was indicated only by this unstructured ellipsis, the omitted description file was incorrectly treated as absent.

A targeted search or a sufficiently large `maxResults` returns the file correctly, so this is not an indexing failure. It is a result-reporting problem: callers can easily mistake a partial result set for a complete inventory.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a directory containing more files than `file_search` displays by default.
2. Place the target file outside the subset selected for display.
3. Call `file_search` with a recursive glob and omit `maxResults`.
4. Observe that the tool reports the total match count, displays only some paths, and appends `...`.
5. Observe that the response provides no structured truncation flag, displayed-result count, or continuation mechanism.

## Actual Behavior

Truncation is represented only by a trailing ellipsis. A matching file omitted from the displayed subset can therefore be mistaken for a nonexistent file.

## Expected Behavior

The response should explicitly state that it is truncated, for example:

```text
Showing 20 of 24 results. Results truncated; narrow the query or increase maxResults.
```

Ideally the tool result would also expose structured metadata such as:

```json
{
  "totalResults": 24,
  "returnedResults": 20,
  "truncated": true
}
```

This would let agents reliably distinguish “no match exists” from “the match may have been omitted.”

## Environment

```
Version: 1.131.0 (user setup)
Commit: e4c7e7b1d6d060162f4aa7f8225271b67ce1df75
```

Modern UI: panel and secondary side bar tabs have no hover background, side bar tabs do
body:
- VS Code Version: 1.130.0 (1b6a188127eeaf9194f945eb6eb89a657e93c54c)
- OS Version: Darwin arm64 27.0.0 (macOS 26.0)
- Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes — the rules involved are core workbench CSS

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable `workbench.experimental.modernUI`.
2. Set `"workbench.activityBar.location": "top"` so the side bar and secondary side bar render their composite bars as icon tabs.
3. Hover a tab in the primary side bar (Explorer / Search / Source Control) — a rounded hover pill appears behind the icon.
4. Hover a tab in the panel (Problems / Output / Terminal), or in the secondary side bar — nothing is painted.

### Expected

All three composite bars give the same hover feedback.

### Actual

Only the primary side bar does.

### Cause

In Modern UI the hover pill is painted on the `.active-item-indicator` child element, in `styleOverrides/browser/media/activityBar.css`:

```css
.style-override .pane-composite-part > .title > .composite-bar-container:not(.dragged-over):not(.dragged-over-head):not(.dragged-over-tail) > .composite-bar > .monaco-action-bar .action-item.icon:not(.checked):hover .active-item-indicator,
.style-override .pane-composite-part > .header-or-footer > .composite-bar-container:not(.dragged-over):not(.dragged-over-head):not(.dragged-over-tail) > .composite-bar > .monaco-action-bar .action-item.icon:not(.checked):hover .active-item-indicator {
	background-color: var(--vscode-list-hoverBackground);
}
```

For the panel and the secondary side bar, though, that element is hidden — same file:

```css
.style-override.monaco-workbench .part.auxiliarybar > .header-or-footer > .composite-bar-container > .composite-bar > .monaco-action-bar .action-item.icon .active-item-indicator,
.style-override.monaco-workbench .pane-composite-part.basepanel > .title > .composite-bar-container > .composite-bar > .monaco-action-bar .action-item.icon .active-item-indicator {
	display: none;
}
```

It is hidden because for those two parts the **active** pill was moved onto `.action-item` itself, in `styleOverrides/browser/media/tabs.css`:

```css
.style-override .part.panel > .title > .composite-bar-container > .composite-bar > .monaco-action-bar .action-item.checked {
	background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--vscode-foreground) 10%, transparent) !important;
}
```

(plus the two equivalent rules for `.part.auxiliarybar > .title` and `> .header-or-footer`.)

The `checked` pill was moved, the `:hover` pill was not. `tabs.css` has no `:hover` rule for these action items, and the one in `activityBar.css` now targets a hidden element — so hovering these tabs paints nothing. The primary side bar keeps its indicator visible and therefore still shows the hover pill.

### Suggested fix

Add the matching hover rule in `tabs.css` for the parts whose indicator is hidden — `.part.panel > .title` and `.part.auxiliarybar > .title | .header-or-footer` — on `.action-item:not(.checked):hover`, using `var(--vscode-list-hoverBackground)` so it stays themable and consistent with the side bar.

### Related

#327267 — same area: the active pill for these tabs is hardcoded and not themable.

title: t1
fix: gate chat tips on registered commands to prevent 'openPlan' command not found (fixes #328231)
body:
### Summary

Clicking the **Plan mode** chat tip throws `command 'workbench.action.chat.openPlan' not found` (bucket `07b425dd-be0d-a662-1409-6bb227df5a7b`, ~1,552 users on 1.131.0). The tip in `chatTipCatalog.ts` renders a markdown link `command:workbench.action.chat.openPlan`, but that command is **not registered** in shipped builds — it only exists on an unmerged feature branch. When the user clicks the rendered link, `openerService` routes it to `commandService._tryExecuteCommand`, which throws because the command is unknown, and the error reaches error telemetry.

The fix is producer-side: the tip service decides which tips are eligible to show, so we gate eligibility on whether every `command:` link the tip renders is actually registered. A tip referencing an unregistered command is never shown, so the dead link is never presented and the error path is never reached. This is general and defends against any future stale command reference in the tip catalog.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#328231
Recommended reviewer: `@meganrogge`

### Culprit Commit

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Commit | `3d374070c9a` (message text later tweaked in `3623d50299a8`) |
| PR | #298271 "improve tip service" |
| Author | `@meganrogge` |
| What it did | Shipped the `tip.planMode` entry referencing `command:workbench.action.chat.openPlan`. The `openPlan` command itself was only added on an unmerged branch (`347fffeb87f`), so it never shipped — leaving the tip pointing at a non-existent command. |

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[ChatTipService shows tip.planMode] --> B[chatTipContentPart renders markdown]
  B --> C[User clicks command:workbench.action.chat.openPlan link]
  C --> D[chatTipContentPart._handleTipAction]
  D --> E[openerService.open]
  E --> F[commandService._tryExecuteCommand]
  F --> G{command registered?}
  G -- no --> H[throw command 'openPlan' not found -> error telemetry]
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role | Evidence |
|------|------|----------|
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatTipCatalog.ts` | Producer of the offending reference | `tip.planMode` renders `command:workbench.action.chat.openPlan`, a command not registered in shipped code |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatTipService.ts` | Eligibility gate (fix location) | `_isEligible` decides which tips are shown; extended to exclude tips with unregistered commands |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatTipContentPart.ts` | Crash-site frame (not modified) | `_handleTipAction` forwards the link to `openerService` |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/commands/common/commandService.ts` | Crash site (not modified) | `_tryExecuteCommand` throws "command not found" |

### Repro Steps

1. Run a shipped 1.131.0 build (where `workbench.action.chat.openPlan` is not registered).
2. Trigger the chat panel such that the Plan mode tip is shown in the tip content part.
3. Click the tip's action link.
4. Observe `command 'workbench.action.chat.openPlan' not found` thrown via `commandService._tryExecuteCommand` and reported to error telemetry.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `chatTipService.ts`: added `_areTipCommandsRegistered(tip)` and a call to it in `_isEligible` before returning `true`. The method builds the tip message, extracts every `command:` id via the existing `extractCommandIds()` helper, and returns `false` (logging a debug line) if any id is missing from `CommandsRegistry.getCommand()`. This fixes the bug at the data producer — the tip service that produces the shown tip — rather than at the crash site in `commandService`. It does not add any `try/catch` and does not remove or alter `logService.error` calls, so the telemetry pipeline is untouched; it simply prevents an invalid tip (one pointing at a non-existent command) from ever being produced. Because `registerAction2` registers into `CommandsRegistry`, this correctly detects all real chat mode-open commands (Ask/Agent/Edit) as registered while excluding the unregistered `openPlan`.

**Alternatives considered**:
- Register a no-op/real `openPlan` command — rejected: the command's real implementation lives on an unmerged branch; shipping a stand-in would mask the missing feature and could mislead users who click it.
- Guard/`try-catch` at `commandService._tryExecuteCommand` — rejected: that is the crash site, not the producer, and swallowing the throw would hide errors from the telemetry pipeline.
- Remove the `tip.planMode` entry outright — rejected: narrower but doesn't prevent the general class of stale command references; the eligibility gate covers this and any future catalog drift.

### Recommended Owner

`@meganrogge` — authored the tip catalog entry and the tip service (commit `3d374070c9a`, PR #298271), and is an active VS Code team member with recent commits in this area (chat/voice). Best positioned to review whether the Plan mode tip should instead ship with a registered command.

title: Agents window Markdown editor: Most of a thematic break maps clicks to the next paragraph
body:
<!-- Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template -->

Testing #326540

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: Insiders with the experimental Markdown editor
- OS Version: macOS
- Audited package revision: microsoft/vscode-packages@1d81418d61ad769f154579196a51a9364c105e2d

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open this Markdown document in **Editing** mode:

   ```markdown
   Before

   ---

   After
   ```

2. While the thematic break is rendered as a horizontal rule, click near its center or right side.

### Expected

Clicking anywhere on the rendered rule activates that block, reveals `---`, and positions the caret at the nearest editable location in the rule.

### Actual

Only clicking near the far-left edge maps into the thematic-break source. Clicking the center or right side moves the caret to the beginning of `After`.

### Impact

Most of the visible rule is a misleading hit target. Users trying to edit or delete the rule are moved into unrelated content and may start typing in the following paragraph.

title: BYOK Chat Completions does not apply Kimi tool-call ID normalization after model switching
body:
I use Qwen and Kimi K2.7 Code as BYOK Custom Endpoint models with the Chat Completions API.

**Observed behavior:**

* Qwen works well when used by itself (served using vLLM).
* Kimi works well when used by itself (served using SGLang).
* If I start an agent conversation with Qwen, let it use tools, and then switch the same conversation to Kimi, Kimi stops or returns no actionable response, after which Copilot reports an error.

I inspected a Kimi-bound request after such a switch. Tool calls from the preceding Qwen turn still used IDs such as:

`chatcmpl-tool-948068bb6570be33`

The call/result pairs were otherwise valid.

**VS Code already has a Kimi history normalizer** that converts outbound IDs to:

`functions.<tool-name>:<global-index>`

It was added specifically for model switching in #325813. However, the BYOK Chat Completions branch constructs its request body directly and does not run the normal `customizeCapiBody` path where this normalization is applied.

I cannot establish from this observation alone that the missing normalization causes the failure. What I can reproduce is that each model works when used alone, while switching from Qwen to Kimi consistently leads to problems.

Regardless of whether it fully explains the observed failure, BYOK should apply the same target-model history normalization as the regular Chat Completions path.

Please apply the existing Kimi tool-call ID normalization to BYOK Chat Completions as well.

title: Add expand/collapse events for folders in the built-in Explorer
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
I'd like to request an API that lets extensions detect when a folder in the built-in VS Code Explorer is expanded or collapsed.

I know that `TreeView` already has `onDidExpandElement` and `onDidCollapseElement`, but, if I understand correctly, those events only work for TreeViews provided by an extension. There doesn't seem to be an equivalent for the standard File Explorer.


## My use case

I'd like to build an extension that automatically collapses the contents of a folder when that folder itself is collapsed.

For example, imagine I have this:
```
project/
└── src/
   ├── components/
   │   ├── buttons/
   │   └── inputs/
   └── utils/
```

If I expand folder `src`, then open several nested folders, and later collapse the `src`, I'd like all of the nested folders recursively under `src` to be collapsed as well.

That way, when I expand `src` again, I see a clean, collapsed `src` folder instead of the previous deeply expanded tree.

This is especially useful in larger projects where the Explorer can quickly become cluttered with many expanded folders.

## Proposed API

I'm not particularly attached to the naming, but something along the lines of:
```js
vscode.window.onDidExpandExplorerItem
vscode.window.onDidCollapseExplorerItem
```
would allow extensions to react to changes in the built-in Explorer.

The event could provide the URI of the affected item, for example:
```js
vscode.window.onDidCollapseExplorerItem(event => {
    console.log(event.uri);
});
```

There may be a better way to expose this that fits the existing API design; the main thing I'm looking for is the ability to observe expand/collapse events from the built-in Explorer.

I've seen this requested a number of times in discussions and feature requests around VS Code, and similar behavior is available in other editors/IDEs. It seems like a relatively small feature that could also enable extensions to provide more useful Explorer navigation and organization features.

I'd be interested in contributing an implementation if this is something the VS Code team would consider adding.

title: Copilot agent terminal commands falsely time out while command has already completed
body:
Type: Bug # Bug report draft: Copilot agent terminal commands falsely time out while command has already completed ## Summary Copilot agent terminal executions intermittently report a timeout/wait state even though the command has already finished and the shell prompt has returned. Pressing Enter in the terminal can clear the wait state. This reproduces with trivial commands. ## Environment - OS: Linux (NixOS) - VS Code: 1.129.1 - Workspace: /home/rconway/nixos - Shell context observed: - Interactive terminal is zsh - Agent command shell was switched to bash via automation profile ## Problem statement When the Copilot agent runs a command and waits for stdout/command completion, the request can remain in a false waiting state. The command is already done and prompt is visible, but the tool reports timeout or appears stuck. ## Reproduction 1. Open Copilot agent in VS Code. 2. Run a silent command such as: - true - printf '' 3. Observe that command output shows completion and shell prompt returns. 4. Agent/tool still sometimes reports timeout/waiting. 5. In some sessions, pressing Enter in the terminal unblocks the wait state. ## Expected behavior - When the command exits and prompt returns, Copilot marks command complete immediately. ## Actual behavior - Copilot intermittently reports timeout/waiting despite command having already completed. ## Diagnostics performed - Sandbox disabled and re-tested: issue still reproduces. - Switched automation shell to bash: issue still reproduces. - Used clean bash args (--noprofile, --norc): issue still reproduces. - Added workaround to force a completion marker on shell EXIT: improved but did not fully resolve. ## Quantified reliability test 20 sequential runs after workaround: - Immediate completion responses: 11 - False-timeout responses: 9 - False-timeout rate: 45% By command type: - Silent success (true): 7 runs, 3 false timeouts - Silent zero-output (printf ''): 2 runs, 2 false timeouts - Silent non-zero (exit 7): 2 runs, 1 false timeout, 1 immediate non-zero completion - Stdout commands: 5 runs, 1 false timeout - Stderr commands: 4 runs, 2 false timeouts ## Workaround attempted Workspace-only workaround added: - Agent automation shell configured to bash with clean args - Non-interactive bash EXIT trap emits completion marker to stderr Files used for workaround in this workspace: - .vscode/settings.json - .vscode/copilot-bash-env.sh This reduced but did not eliminate false timeouts. ## Impact - Agent appears hung for common command flows. - Requires manual intervention (press Enter / poll terminal output), reducing trust and automation reliability. ## Suspected area Terminal completion/idle detection race or prompt-return detection in Copilot terminal bridge, especially for low-output or no-output command exits. ## Requested fix - Treat process exit as authoritative completion even with no stdout. - Improve idle/prompt detection for silent exits. - Avoid requiring additional terminal input after completed commands. ## Optional additional details to include before submitting -
